key_insight: Enforcing linear completeness gives problem-independent machine learning (PIML) finite element spaces a convergence guarantee that rigid-body displacement invariance alone does not provide.
engineering_relevance: PIML can accelerate substructure-based finite element analysis by learning reusable numerical shape functions while preserving conformity and controlling approximation error.
method: Bound PIML error using finite element discretization error and network generalization error.
Reconstruct transition-matrix columns using linear displacement constraints to reproduce linear polynomials.
Derive H1- and L2-norm error estimates and convergence results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments supporting optimal convergence rates, good generalization, and numerical stability, but gives no quantitative results.
watch_item: Linear completeness addresses mesh-refinement convergence, but accuracy still depends on network generalization for the material distributions and geometries encountered.
paper_title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
